jobs.title: AI GPU Arch Perf Analysis Intern
jobs.description:
Job Details: Job Description: As an AI Architecture Performance Analysis Graduate Intern, you will join Intel's GPU Compute Architecture team and contribute to core GPU kernel perf analysis using real AI workloads.
Your work will directly support hardware/software co design and help analyze and shape the performance of next generation Intel GPU and AI accelerator platforms, while giving you hands on exposure to GPU architecture and low level performance engineering.

Key Responsibilities
•	Analyze and optimize core GPU compute kernels for AI and numerical workloads (e.g., GEMM, Attention, operator fusion).
•	Reproduce representative AI inference and training workloads for GPU IP validation.
•	Perform GPU performance profiling and analysis to identify compute, memory, and pipeline bottlenecks.
•	Build performance profiles and models to understand architecture level performance behavior.
•	Provide workload and kernel level insights to support GPU architecture design and HW/SW co design efforts. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications
•	Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
•	Proficiency in Python for analysis, experimentation, or tooling.
•	Solid understanding of AI fundamentals, including common models and algorithms.
•	Strong interest in GPU architecture, GPU programming, parallel computing, and performance optimization.
•	Basic knowledge of computer systems, such as CPU/GPU architecture, memory systems, and performance analysis.

Preferred Qualifications
•	Experience with GPU kernels or programming models (e.g., CUDA, OpenCL, SYCL, Triton).
•	Exposure to performance optimization, compiler, or parallel computing coursework, research, or internships.
•	Strong analytical and problem solving skills, with the ability to reason from profiling data.
•	Interest in AI systems and infrastructure, beyond model level development.
•	Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, cross functional engineering environment. jobs.title: Compiler Engineering Intern
jobs.description: Job Details: Job Description: Join Us in Shaping the Future At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities. The Team The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered. Position Overview We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype. Responsibilities •	Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies. •	Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase. •	Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions. •	Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project. •	Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members. •	Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team. •	Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications •	Currently pursuing a Bachelor or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline. •	Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area. •	Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems. •	Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions. Preferred Qualifications •	Hands-on experience with LLVM or related compiler infrastructure, including front-end development, intermediate representations, optimization passes, code generation, runtimes, or debug information. •	Research or development experience involving CPU/GPU architectures, heterogeneous computing, AI/ML compilation, HPC, parallel programming, or performance optimization. •	Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem. •	Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. •	Tile-base programming model knowledge •	GPU Compute kernel writing experience •	Experience contributing to open-source software or working in a large collaborative codebase. •	Publications, technical reports, patents, open-source contributions, or other evidence of advanced technical work. Success in This Role •	Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies. •	Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills. •	Clear written and verbal communication. •	Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed. •	Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering. jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern
jobs.description: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics.   KLA's Central Engineering organization is made up of nine Centers of Excellence (CoEs) spanning disciplines like automation, motion control, sensors, platform design, and packaging. Each CoE contributes not only technical deliverables but also deep expertise, best practices, and advanced tools that elevate both what we build—and how we build it. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. 1.	Participate in company training on relevant software technologies, development tools, and processes. Provide regular work reports and updates. 2.	Software Development Projects: Contribute to the rapid prototype development and testing of semiconductor equipment software for inspection, metrology and data analysis systems. Existing code analysis, refactoring and performance optimization. 3.	Test Automation Projects: Participate in developing tools for automated testing, deployment, and operations based on CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery) processes. 4.	Work at least 3 full days per week, following standard company working hours. 5.	Outstanding performance during the internship may lead to a full-time offer through campus recruitment. Minimum Qualifications 1.	Currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate student in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electronics, Physics, Automation, Mathematics, or related fields. 2.	Familiar with programming languages and frameworks, including but not limited to: C/C++/C#/Python/Java/JavaScript/Vue/AngularJS/PHP. 3.	Solid knowledge of CS and SW engineering: DSA, multithreading, OOP, design patterns, etc. 4.	Experience with projects related to AI / LLM / AI Agents is preferred. 5.	Strong problem-solving, analytical, and debugging skills. 6.	Fluent in English, with good communication skills, teamwork spirit, and a proactive, self-driven attitude. About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. Use of AI Statement At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset. We offer a competitive, family friendly total rewards package. We design our programs to reflect our commitment to an inclusive environment, while ensuring we provide benefits that meet the diverse needs of our employees. KLA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.
